title: Disentangling the percepts of illusory movement and sensory stimulation during tendon vibration in the EEG
description: This dataset contains 16-channel sensorimotor EEG recordings from twenty healthy right-handed adults receiving tendon vibration on the left arm. Vibration of the biceps and triceps tendons at different frequencies either induced an illusion of elbow extension or produced only a vibration sensation (control). The data allow the neural correlates of illusory movement to be separated from those of sensory stimulation.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.tec Nautilus wireless amplifier at 500 Hz using 16 electrodes over the sensorimotor cortex (10-10 system), with a 0.1-100 Hz hardware bandpass filter and a right earlobe reference. Tendon vibration was delivered with Vibramoov vibrators on the distal biceps and triceps tendons of the left arm. Illusion trials used 90 Hz (biceps) and 50 Hz (triceps), and control trials used 70 Hz on both tendons. Each 3 s stimulus had a 1 s ramp-up, 1 s stable phase and 1 s ramp-down. Each participant completed three blocks of 72 randomized vibrations (36 illusion, 36 control), with inter-stimulus intervals of 1-3 s.
